stem: A client with a viral syndrome has an elevated absolute lymphocyte count. How should the nurse interpret this finding?

options.A: Reactive lymphocytosis is compatible with viral infection, but the finding should be interpreted with the clinical picture and other hematologic data.
options.B: Lymphocytosis establishes an acute bacterial infection and by itself provides sufficient evidence that antibacterial treatment is indicated.
options.C: An elevated lymphocyte count establishes a hematologic malignancy without requiring review of symptoms, smear findings, or other blood counts.
options.D: Lymphocytosis has no recognized association with infectious illness and therefore should be interpreted independently of the client's viral syndrome.

rationale: Current NCBI/StatPearls guidance describes lymphocytosis as a common hematologic abnormality with a broad differential. Viral infections are common causes of reactive lymphocytosis, but infectious, inflammatory, physiologic, and clonal/malignant causes must be distinguished using history, examination, CBC context, trends, and when indicated peripheral-smear or further testing. Therefore A is correct. B incorrectly makes lymphocytosis diagnostic of bacterial infection and an antibiotic indication, C incorrectly makes it diagnostic of malignancy, and D denies its well-established association with viral infections.
educational_objective: Interpret lymphocytosis in clinical context, recognizing viral infection as a common reactive cause without overdiagnosing from a single differential count.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (StatPearls)
source_version_date: Leukocytosis last update June 15, 2026; Lymphocytosis in StatPearls 2026 edition; live NCBI pages retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Leukocytosis: lymphocytosis is often seen in viral infection and interpretation requires age, clinical history, differential counts, trends, and associated CBC abnormalities. Lymphocytosis Etiology/Pearls: viral infections are common reactive causes; evaluation uses history, exam, smear, and selected further testing to distinguish reactive from clonal causes.
source_claim_supported: Viral infections commonly cause reactive lymphocytosis, but lymphocytosis is nonspecific and requires clinical and hematologic correlation rather than serving as a stand-alone diagnosis.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor and interpret diagnostic/laboratory results and recognize changes in client condition.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only absolute wording and balanced all alternatives as parallel interpretations of lymphocytosis.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — current NCBI guidance directly supports viral reactive lymphocytosis and a broad differential requiring correlation; A uniquely preserves both facts.
